name: Zohran Mamdani
bio: Zohran Mamdani is the Mayor of New York City, elected in 2025 as a Democratic Socialist from Queens. He has championed affordable housing, rent relief, and free public transit. A first-generation American of Ugandan-Indian descent, Mamdani built his career on tenant rights and economic justice before his historic mayoral win.
summary: NYC Mayor elected in 2025 — a Democratic Socialist from Queens running on affordable housing, free transit, and tenant protections.

positions.description: Supports universal rent control, expanded public housing, and deep affordability requirements on new construction.
Advocates for a city-level public option and expanded mental health services.
Backs aggressive decarbonization of city buildings and free public transit to reduce car dependency.
Supports cutting the NYPD budget and reinvesting in social services and community programs.
Backs fully funded public schools, universal pre-K, and free college programs.
Strong sanctuary city advocate; opposes cooperation with federal immigration enforcement.
Supports taxing the wealthy to fund public services; backs a city pied-à-terre tax on luxury second homes.
Central to his campaign: make NYC buses and subways free for all riders.
Advocates for stronger worker protections, higher minimum wage, and curbing corporate landlords.

name: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez
bio: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez is the U.S. Representative for New York's 14th congressional district, covering parts of the Bronx and Queens. First elected in 2018 at age 29 as the youngest woman ever elected to Congress, she is a leading voice of the progressive left and a co-author of the Green New Deal.
summary: Progressive U.S. Representative for the Bronx/Queens who co-authored the Green New Deal and champions Medicare for All and economic justice.

positions.description: Co-sponsors federal legislation for universal rent control and expanded public housing investments.
Lead advocate for Medicare for All — a single-payer system replacing private insurance.
Co-author of the Green New Deal; supports 100% clean energy by 2030 and massive federal green investment.
Advocates for defunding and restructuring police departments; redirect funds to mental health and community services.
Supports canceling student debt, tuition-free public college, and fully funding K-12 schools.
Strongly pro-immigration reform; has been vocal critic of ICE detention conditions.
Proposes a 70% marginal tax rate on income above $10 million to fund social programs.
Supports federal investment in public transit infrastructure and electrification.
Advocates for a federal $15+ minimum wage, workers' rights, and antitrust enforcement on corporations.

name: Mike Lawler
bio: Mike Lawler is the Republican U.S. Representative for New York's 17th congressional district, covering Rockland County and parts of Westchester. First elected in 2022, he is a moderate Republican known for his focus on constituent services, local infrastructure, and cross-aisle collaboration on select issues.
summary: Moderate Republican U.S. Representative for Rockland/Westchester who focuses on local infrastructure, fiscal responsibility, and constituent services.

positions.description: Favors reducing regulatory burdens on builders and incentivizing private development over government mandates.
Supports preserving private insurance options and market competition; opposes government-run single-payer.
Supports some environmental protections but opposes policies that would significantly raise energy costs.
Strong supporter of law enforcement funding; opposes defunding or major restructuring of police departments.
Supports local control of schools and parental choice including charter and private school options.
Supports securing the southern border and enforcing immigration laws; more moderate than many in his party on pathways for existing residents.
Advocates for restoring the SALT deduction cap and reducing overall tax burdens on middle-class families.
Supports federal infrastructure investment but was a vocal critic of NYC congestion pricing.
Favors reducing business regulations to spur economic growth and job creation in the Hudson Valley region.

name: Kathy Hochul
bio: Kathy Hochul is the 57th Governor of New York, the first woman to hold the office. She assumed the governorship in August 2021 and was elected to a full term in 2022. A moderate Democrat, she focuses on economic development, housing production, and public safety while navigating the progressive wing of her party.
summary: New York's first female Governor — a moderate Democrat focused on housing production, economic growth, and public safety across the state.

positions.description: Has pushed major housing production plans including the New York Housing Compact, requiring new units near transit hubs.
Expanded Medicaid coverage and mental health services statewide; supports the ACA framework.
Signed the CLCPA into law; committed to 70% renewable energy by 2030 and 100% zero-emission electricity by 2040.
Increased state police presence for public safety concerns; more centrist than progressive wing on criminal justice reform.
Signed substantial increases in Foundation Aid for public schools and supports early childhood education expansion.
Supports immigrant communities and opposes federal deportation operations; has pushed for migrant housing solutions.
Resisted calls for new wealth taxes while supporting targeted tax credits for working families.
Major champion of MTA capital plans; initially paused then partially restored congestion pricing.
Focuses on attracting business investment to upstate NY and diversifying the state economy beyond NYC.

name: Kirsten Gillibrand
bio: Kirsten Gillibrand is the senior U.S. Senator from New York, serving since 2009. She has been a leading advocate for military sexual assault survivors, the 9/11 Victims Compensation Fund, and paid family leave. Originally elected as a moderate House Democrat, she has moved progressively left over her career.
summary: Senior U.S. Senator for New York who led the fight for 9/11 first responders, military sexual assault reforms, and paid family leave.

positions.description: Supports federal investment in affordable housing construction and tenant protections.
Co-sponsors Medicare for All and has advocated for expanding mental health parity in insurance coverage.
Strong supporter of the Green New Deal and aggressive federal clean energy standards.
Supports the George Floyd Justice in Policing Act and systemic accountability measures.
Advocates for free community college, student debt relief, and increased funding for Title I schools.
Supports a pathway to citizenship for undocumented immigrants and DACA protections.
Supports raising taxes on corporations and the wealthy to fund social programs.
Supports federal transit infrastructure funding; backed the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law.
Supports stronger Wall Street regulations and consumer financial protections.

name: Chuck Schumer
bio: Chuck Schumer is the junior U.S. Senator from New York and Senate Minority Leader, having served since 1999. One of the most powerful figures in American politics, he led Democrats through the passage of the Inflation Reduction Act, the CHIPS Act, and the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law.
summary: Senate Minority Leader and New York's junior Senator — a pragmatic dealmaker who shepherded the Inflation Reduction Act and CHIPS Act into law.

positions.description: Supports federal funding for affordable housing construction and expanded rental assistance programs.
Led passage of ACA protections and prescription drug price negotiation provisions in the Inflation Reduction Act.
Shepherded the Inflation Reduction Act — the largest climate investment in US history — through the Senate.
Supports some accountability measures but takes a more centrist position focused on community policing over structural overhaul.
Supports increased federal education funding, Pell Grant expansion, and vocational training programs.
Backs comprehensive immigration reform with a pathway to citizenship; has negotiated bipartisan border security deals.
Led passage of minimum corporate tax and IRS funding increases in the Inflation Reduction Act.
Secured billions in transit funding through the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law for NYC and statewide systems.
Supports antitrust enforcement, tech regulation, and domestic manufacturing through the CHIPS Act.

name: Hakeem Jeffries
bio: Hakeem Jeffries is the U.S. Representative for New York's 8th congressional district covering Brooklyn and Queens, and the House Minority Leader since 2023. The first Black lawmaker to lead a party in Congress, he is a pragmatic progressive and rising national figure in the Democratic Party.
summary: House Minority Leader and Brooklyn/Queens Representative — a pragmatic progressive and the first Black party leader in Congress.

positions.description: Supports federal affordable housing funding, tenant protections, and anti-displacement measures in rapidly gentrifying districts.
Supports expanding the ACA, lowering prescription drug costs, and protecting Medicaid from cuts.
Backed the Inflation Reduction Act's climate provisions; supports clean energy investment and environmental justice.
Supports the George Floyd Justice in Policing Act and accountability measures, while opposing the 'defund' framing.
Advocates for increased Title I funding, free pre-K, and expanded college access programs.
Supports a pathway to citizenship, DACA protections, and humane asylum processes.
Supports raising taxes on corporations and wealthy individuals to fund social investment.
Supported the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law's transit provisions; advocates for MTA capital investment.
Supports worker protections, antitrust enforcement, and domestic manufacturing initiatives.

name: Elise Stefanik
bio: Elise Stefanik is the U.S. Representative for New York's 21st congressional district covering the North Country and Adirondacks. Once considered a moderate Republican, she shifted hard right after 2020 to become a leading Trump ally and House Republican Conference Chair. She was nominated as UN Ambassador in 2025.
summary: Trump-aligned Republican Representative for Upstate NY's North Country and House Republican Conference Chair, nominated as UN Ambassador.

positions.description: Supports reducing federal regulatory burdens on housing development; opposes government-mandated affordability programs.
Strongly opposes Medicare for All; supports market competition and protecting private insurance options.
Has shifted from moderate positions to skepticism of climate mandates; prioritizes energy independence over aggressive decarbonization.
Strongly pro-law enforcement; opposes any defunding or structural reform of police departments.
Supports parental rights in education and school choice; has pushed back on progressive curriculum debates.
Supports strict border enforcement, reduced immigration levels, and has promoted replacement theory-adjacent rhetoric.
Supports extending the TCJA tax cuts and reducing regulatory and tax burdens on rural businesses and families.
Supports rural infrastructure investment; limited positions on urban transit.
Supports deregulation and energy production in the North Country to drive economic growth.

name: Dan Goldman
bio: Dan Goldman is the U.S. Representative for New York's 10th congressional district covering Lower Manhattan and parts of Brooklyn. A former federal prosecutor who led the first impeachment inquiry of Donald Trump in 2019, he won a crowded 2022 primary and is known for his focus on democracy, rule of law, and social investment.
summary: Democratic Representative for Lower Manhattan and Brooklyn — former federal prosecutor who led Trump's first impeachment inquiry.

positions.description: Supports expanding affordable housing production and tenant protections in some of NYC's most expensive neighborhoods.
Supports expanding healthcare access, protecting the ACA, and lowering prescription drug prices.
Backed the Inflation Reduction Act's climate investments; supports NYC's Local Law 97 building emissions standards.
Supports accountability measures and the George Floyd Justice in Policing Act; opposes the 'defund' framing.
Advocates for increased public school funding, pre-K expansion, and student debt relief.
Strongly pro-immigration reform; supports a pathway to citizenship and humane asylum processes.
Supports raising taxes on corporations and the ultra-wealthy to fund public services and reduce inequality.
Strong supporter of MTA investment, congestion pricing, and expanding transit access in his district.
Given his prosecutorial background, strongly supports financial regulation, antitrust enforcement, and corporate accountability.

name: Adriano Espaillat
bio: Adriano Espaillat is the U.S. Representative for New York's 13th congressional district, covering Harlem, Washington Heights, and parts of the Bronx. The first Dominican American elected to Congress, he previously served in the NY State Senate and is a progressive voice on immigration and economic justice.
summary: Progressive Democratic Representative for Harlem and Washington Heights — the first Dominican American elected to Congress.

positions.description: Advocates for expanded public housing investment, universal rent stabilization, and anti-displacement protections in his district.
Co-sponsors Medicare for All; has pushed for expanded community health center funding in Harlem and the Bronx.
Supports the Green New Deal and environmental justice measures targeting pollution in frontline communities.
Supports cutting the NYPD budget and reinvesting in social services; backed the George Floyd Justice in Policing Act.
Champions CUNY funding increases, free community college, and bilingual education programs.
One of Congress's leading voices on immigration reform; supports a pathway to citizenship and opposes ICE enforcement in schools and hospitals.
Supports progressive taxation on corporations and the wealthy to fund housing, healthcare, and education.
Supports MTA investment and free transit for low-income riders; backed congestion pricing.
Advocates for a $20+ federal minimum wage, stronger worker protections, and antitrust action against corporate consolidation.

name: Nydia Velázquez
bio: Nydia Velázquez is the U.S. Representative for New York's 7th congressional district covering Brooklyn, Queens, and Lower Manhattan. The first Puerto Rican woman elected to Congress in 1992, she serves on the House Financial Services Committee and Small Business Committee and is a progressive champion for working families.
summary: The first Puerto Rican woman elected to Congress, representing Brooklyn and Queens since 1992 as a progressive champion for small businesses and workers.

positions.description: Long-time advocate for affordable housing, public housing funding, and tenant protections in rapidly gentrifying neighborhoods.
Supports Medicare for All and has fought to protect Medicaid and community health centers.
Backs the Green New Deal and environmental justice; has focused on climate resilience in coastal Brooklyn.
Supports accountability legislation and reinvesting police funds into social services.
Advocates for free community college, Pell Grant expansion, and bilingual education funding.
Champion of immigration reform, DACA protections, and the rights of undocumented workers in New York.
Supports raising taxes on the wealthy and corporations; backed the minimum corporate tax in the Inflation Reduction Act.
Supports federal transit investment; has secured funds for bus and subway improvements in her district.
As Small Business Committee Ranking Member, focuses on small business access to capital, minority-owned businesses, and worker rights.

name: George Latimer
bio: George Latimer is the U.S. Representative for New York's 16th congressional district, having defeated progressive incumbent Jamaal Bowman in a 2024 primary. A former Westchester County Executive and long-time state legislator, he is a moderate Democrat focused on constituent services, fiscal responsibility, and pragmatic governance.
summary: Moderate Democratic Representative for the Bronx and Westchester, former County Executive who defeated Squad member Jamaal Bowman in 2024.

positions.description: Supports housing production with practical, market-compatible affordability requirements rather than aggressive government mandates.
Supports expanding the ACA and protecting Medicaid; more cautious than progressives on single-payer.
Supports clean energy investment and environmental protection; more moderate than his predecessor on the pace of transition.
Supports accountability measures and community policing; rejects the defund framing and prioritizes public safety.
Supports increased public school funding and college affordability; more pragmatic approach than bold free-college proposals.
Supports a pathway to citizenship and humane immigration policy; rejects the most aggressive enforcement positions.
Moderate position; supports some progressive tax measures while being mindful of impacts on middle-class and small-business taxpayers.
Supports transit investment as a Westchester resident; backed the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law.
Pragmatic moderate who supports both worker protections and business-friendly policies to grow the local economy.

name: Letitia James
bio: Letitia James is the New York State Attorney General since 2019 and the first Black woman elected to statewide office in New York. Known for her aggressive legal actions against Donald Trump, the NRA, and major corporations, she is a progressive Democrat from Brooklyn who was widely seen as a potential gubernatorial candidate.
summary: New York Attorney General and first Black woman elected to statewide NY office — known for landmark legal actions against Trump and the NRA.

positions.description: Has pursued landlords and developers for predatory practices; supports tenant protections and affordable housing production.
Has sued pharmaceutical companies over drug pricing; supports expanding Medicaid and mental health access.
Has pursued fossil fuel companies for climate damages; supports aggressive clean energy transition.
Led the state investigation into NYPD conduct; supports accountability and systemic reform.
Supports equitable school funding and free college access; has defended CUNY against budget cuts.
Consistently defended immigrant rights; has taken legal action against federal immigration enforcement overreach.
Supports progressive taxation and has targeted wealthy tax evaders through the AG's office.
Supports MTA investment and has taken legal action to protect transit workers' rights.
Known for aggressive antitrust and consumer protection enforcement; has taken on big tech, Wall Street, and predatory lenders.

name: Mark Levine
bio: Mark Levine is the New York City Comptroller, elected in 2021. A former Manhattan Borough President and City Council member, he is a progressive Democrat who oversees the city's finances, pension funds, and audits city agencies. He has been a vocal advocate for affordable housing, climate investment, and fiscal transparency.
summary: NYC Comptroller and former Manhattan Borough President — a progressive Democrat overseeing the city's finances and pension funds.

positions.description: Champions affordable housing construction, tenant protections, and using city pension funds to invest in affordable housing.
Supports expanding mental health services and city-funded healthcare access for uninsured New Yorkers.
Advocates for divesting city pension funds from fossil fuels and investing in green infrastructure.
Has audited NYPD spending; supports reallocating police resources toward social services and mental health response.
Supports increased education funding and has audited school spending to improve equity across districts.
Supports sanctuary city policies and city services for immigrant communities.
Supports progressive taxation to fund city services; has pushed for greater transparency on city tax expenditures.
Supports MTA investment and has advocated for city pension funds to invest in transit infrastructure.
Focuses on corporate accountability, responsible contracting, and protecting workers through the comptroller's office.

name: Jumaane Williams
bio: Jumaane Williams is the New York City Public Advocate, first elected in 2019 and re-elected in 2021. A progressive Democrat from Brooklyn, he serves as a watchdog over city agencies and an ombudsman for residents. He ran for Governor in 2022 and is known for his bold positions on police accountability, housing, and social justice.
summary: NYC Public Advocate and progressive Brooklyn Democrat — a watchdog for city residents known for bold stances on police accountability and housing.

positions.description: Champions right-to-shelter, anti-eviction protections, and significant increases in affordable housing construction.
Supports universal healthcare access and has advocated for expanded mental health crisis response as an alternative to police.
Supports aggressive climate action, Local Law 97 enforcement, and environmental justice for frontline communities.
One of NYC's most vocal police accountability advocates; supports cutting the NYPD budget and investing in mental health response teams.
Champions equitable school funding, restorative justice in schools, and free higher education.
Strongly supports sanctuary city policies and immigrant rights; has pushed back against federal enforcement operations.
Supports higher taxes on the wealthy and corporations to fund housing, healthcare, and social services.
Supports free or reduced-fare public transit and significant MTA investment.
Advocates for a living wage, strong worker protections, and corporate accountability in city contracting.

name: Antonio Delgado
bio: Antonio Delgado is the Lieutenant Governor of New York, appointed in 2022 when then-Lt. Governor Brian Benjamin resigned. A former U.S. Representative for New York's 19th district and Rhodes Scholar, Delgado is a moderate progressive who focuses on rural economic development, healthcare access, and democracy reform.
summary: New York Lieutenant Governor and former Congressman — a moderate progressive focused on rural communities, healthcare, and economic development.

positions.description: Supports affordable housing investment and has focused on rural housing challenges across upstate New York.
Champions rural healthcare access, Medicaid expansion, and community health center funding.
Supports clean energy investment and has focused on agricultural sustainability and rural clean energy opportunities.
Supports accountability and community policing reforms; more centrist than the progressive wing on structural change.
Supports equitable school funding, rural broadband for remote learning, and college affordability.
Supports a pathway to citizenship and humane immigration policy; focused on farmworker rights in upstate New York.
Moderate position; supports targeted tax relief for working families while maintaining fiscal responsibility.
Supports infrastructure investment including rural transit and broadband connectivity across the state.
Focuses on rural economic development, small business support, and diversifying upstate New York's economy.

name: Thomas DiNapoli
bio: Thomas DiNapoli is the New York State Comptroller, serving since 2007. A former Assemblymember from Long Island, he oversees the state's $280 billion pension fund — one of the largest in the country — and audits state agencies. He is known for his fiscal prudence, transparency initiatives, and push to divest the pension fund from fossil fuels.
summary: New York State Comptroller since 2007 — oversees the state's $280 billion pension fund and state agency audits.

positions.description: Supports affordable housing investment and has used the state pension fund to invest in community development financial institutions.
Supports expanding Medicaid and has scrutinized healthcare cost growth through state audits.
Champion of fossil fuel divestment for the state pension fund; has pushed for ESG investment standards.
Focuses on fiscal accountability of police budgets rather than taking strong stances on reform vs. funding.
Supports equitable education funding and has audited school district spending to improve transparency.
Supports immigrant communities and has included immigrant workforce data in state economic reports.
Focuses on fiscal responsibility and sustainability; supports progressive revenue measures paired with spending discipline.
Has audited MTA finances and supports transparent capital investment in transit infrastructure.
Uses the pension fund as a corporate governance tool; pushes companies to adopt responsible labor and environmental practices.
